questions.statement: I write with my ________ in my notebook.
questions.context: Scenario about school-places in a Colombian school or city context.

options.feedback: Incorrect. A desk is a piece of furniture that you sit at, not something you hold in your hand to write.
Correct! A pencil is the tool you grip in your hand to write inside a notebook.
Incorrect. The board is the large flat surface the teacher writes on, not the instrument in your hand.
Incorrect. A window is part of the wall of the classroom and has nothing to do with writing on paper.

questions.explanation:
This question evaluates the student's ability to remember the topic of School Places and Objects at an A2 level. It focuses on Colombian contexts and standard A2 grammar.

options.feedback: Incorrect. Here "study" means to go to lessons at school, and a bed belongs to the bedroom at home.

questions.statement: What do you use to erase a mistake?
questions.context: Scenario about school-places in a Colombian school or city context.

options.feedback: Incorrect. A sharpener trims a pencil to a point, so it cannot rub graphite off the page.
Incorrect. A ruler measures length and draws straight lines, so it cannot remove anything.
Correct! An eraser is the tool whose whole purpose is to rub out pencil marks on a page.
Incorrect. A book holds printed pages to read, and rubbing it would only smear the ink.

questions.explanation:
This question evaluates the student's ability to understand the topic of School Places and Objects at an A2 level. It focuses on Colombian contexts and standard A2 grammar.

questions.statement: I carry my books in my ________.
questions.context: Scenario about school-places in a Colombian school or city context.

options.feedback: Incorrect. A wallet is small and holds money and cards, so it cannot carry books.
Incorrect. A pencil case is a small pouch for writing tools, not for books.
Correct! A backpack is designed to be worn on the back and to carry books and school supplies.
Incorrect. A pocket holds small items such as keys, and a book is far too large for it.

This question evaluates the student's ability to apply the topic of School Places and Objects at an A2 level. It focuses on Colombian contexts and standard A2 grammar.

questions.statement: What do you use to draw a straight line?
questions.context: Scenario about school-places in a Colombian school or city context.

options.feedback: Correct! A ruler has two straight parallel edges, and you draw against one of them to keep the line straight.
Incorrect. Scissors cut paper or fabric, and in English this would be "a pair of scissors".
Incorrect. A pen does make a line, but with no straight edge as a guide the line can drift and curve.
Incorrect. Glue joins two surfaces together, and in English this would be "some glue".

questions.explanation:
This question evaluates the student's ability to analyze the topic of School Places and Objects at an A2 level. It focuses on Colombian contexts and standard A2 grammar.

questions.statement: We eat lunch in the school ________.
questions.context: Scenario about school-places in a Colombian school or city context.

options.feedback: Correct! "Cafeteria" is the word for the place in a school where students buy and eat their midday meal.
Incorrect. An office is where the teachers and the staff work, and students do not eat their lunch there.
Incorrect. A library is for reading and borrowing books, and eating is not allowed in it.
Incorrect. A bus is a vehicle rather than a place, and the noun after "the school" must name a room or a building.

questions.explanation:
This question evaluates the student's ability to analyze the topic of School Places and Objects at an A2 level. It focuses on Colombian contexts and standard A2 grammar.

questions.context: Scenario about school-places in a Colombian school or city context.

options.feedback: Incorrect. A lab is equipped for science experiments, and its shelves hold equipment rather than a collection of books.
Incorrect. A closet is a small storage space for coats and cleaning supplies, not a place to keep a library.
Incorrect. A playground is an open outdoor space for sport, and it holds no books at all.
Correct! A library is the room in a school built to store a large collection of books and to lend them out.
